items.text: Hello again, Pool Fans!
Pure Pool Pro Hotfix #4 is now live on PC & Console. Please update your game for the best possible experience.

This update is a small, focused quality-of-life pass, aimed squarely at smoothing out local multiplayer, online stat tracking, and match resolution logic, while also tightening up some other areas and the rare but notorious "Cueing Discrepancy" bug.

notes.title: Local Play Now Supports a 2nd Controller

items.text: Local matches now support two controllers - one per player - instead of relying solely on pass-the-pad.

With Hotfix 4, players can now connect and use a second controller in supported local game types, giving each player direct control on their own pad. Many of you who have asked for a more “couch‑friendly” setup should now find local sessions feel closer to a traditional head‑to‑head experience.
Your Player Card should now correctly display online-only stats. These stats combine both Ranked and Versus performance rather than including matches played in offline modes.
Previously, stats displayed here incorrectly included stats that combined online and offline modes and/or failed to update as expected. With this hotfix:
Online Versus and Ranked wins, losses and related stats should update more reliably.
Player Cards will more accurately represent your current online record.
If you've been grinding competitive matches and not seeing that reflected in your card, this should now be resolved.

Important Note: your online stats will display as 0 until connecting to our servers for the first time after the patch goes live. If the game is launched offline you will need to connect to the internet in order for your stats to sync. This is because online stats are now held on the server to ensure wins and losses are attributed correctly, even when disconnecting during a match.

We’ve finally found a fix for a known online desync issue which caused drifting cues / odd cue ball behaviour. Thank you for your patience and for your detailed reports on this one; it was notoriously difficult to pinpoint the issue as it would only ever occur on the live build!
We’ve fixed a bug that would occasionally mess with how online results are handled when an opponent disconnects.
In rare cases, a win could be incorrectly attributed if an opponent disconnected at specific points in a match. The underlying logic has been updated so that:
Match results are aligned with the intended outcome
Disconnect scenarios are processed in a fairer and more predictable way
Our goal here is to reduce edge-case frustration in online play and ensure your record better reflects what actually happened on the table.
Alongside the above, Hotfix 4 includes a series of smaller polish passes and improvements:
UI refinements across menus and match presentation
Subtle audio tweaks for clearer, more consistent feedback
Minor graphical adjustments for improved overall visual cohesion
Individually these are small changes, but together they should help Pure Pool Pro feel just that little bit smoother and more joined‑up.
Thank you again for your continued detailed feedback on Pure Pool Pro - from local play and online behaviour to UI presentation.
OTHER PURE POOL PRO NEWS...
Pure Pool Pro - Xbox Series X|S launches 23.07.2026
Pure Pool Pro - Snooker Expansion Pack now in full development.
Pure Pool Pro - US 8-Ball Community Tournament in August; Discord Moderator Aurakite is running this - you have just 2 weeks left to enter, here: SIGN UP FOR COMMUNITY TOURNAMENT
As always, every report, post, and note helps us decide what to address next - so keep it coming!
We’ll see you at the table.
The Pure Pool Pro Team 🎱

notes.title: Pure Pool Pro | Controller Vibration & DualSense Haptics Update - Now Live

items.text: With today’s update, we’ve introduced Controller Vibration on PC and full DualSense Haptic Feedback on PS5. We hope this makes Pure Pool Pro feel that little bit more tactile, satisfying, and immersive.
This update is live now on PC and PlayStation 5.
On PC, players using supported game controllers - including the DualSense - will now experience new force feedback vibration effects during gameplay and in menus.
Vibration when striking the cue ball
Vibration feedback while navigating UI menus
Cue-to-cue ball vibration will vary in intensity and duration depending on the power of your shot.
The goal here is to make each shot feel a little more physical and responsive in your hands.
Please note: this is a PS5-exclusive feature. PC players who use the DualSense Controller will only experience the standard “PC - Controller Vibration Support” described above.
On PlayStation 5, we’ve implemented full DualSense haptics, which includes the use of the controller speaker for additional sensory feedback.
Enhanced cue-to-cue ball contact feedback
Enhanced Money Shot heartbeat effects
UI navigation haptics
Additional immersive sound effects played through the DualSense speaker
On PS5, cue strike feedback also varies in intensity and duration depending on the on-shot power, with the addition of some dynamic SFX from the DualSense’s built-in speaker.
This should make shot impacts feel that bit more expressive and immersive, especially during those high-pressure moments!
If you’d rather keep things vibration-free, that’s totally fine! You can switch these features off at any time:
PC / Steam → via your controller or Steam input settings
PS5 → via your system's DualSense settings (you can adjust the controller speaker volume to your liking here, too).

notes.title: Make Sure You Update Before You Play

items.text: Be sure to update the game before your next session to make sure you’re getting the best possible experience. We hope Vibration/Haptics add a satisfying layer to every break, pot, and pressure shot.
We’re now continuing our work on Patch 3 and hope to share concrete details of what this will include soon.
We’ll see you at the table!
The Pure Pool Pro Team
Pure Pool Pro Patch 3 arrives Thursday, 21st May.

Our most substantial patch yet introduces ranked matchmaking, fairer starts with Lag for Break, the long‑requested Push Out rule for 9-Ball, online stability improvements, and a major visual fix that’s been on our hit list since launch.

notes.title: Ranked Game Mode - Global Leaderboards & More Competitive Focus

items.text: “Quick Game” will now evolve into our new Ranked Game experience.
Global Leaderboards for each online game mode
Separate rankings for all three difficulties
When selecting “Any” as your game type, you’ll also see an overall ranking board of your performance across all ranked matches at all difficulties.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/038de95ada3d1b812cb942f7c642f0ad9809eea8.gif"]
Whether you’re grinding 8-Ball, mastering 9-Ball, or mixing it up across modes and difficulties, you’ll now have a clear way to measure your progress against the global player base.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/3e6d28981ee1a9dac9f359e5d59fa68512334441.gif"]
Our goal here is to ramp up the competitive layer of Pure Pool Pro, give you more reasons to keep coming back, and make every rack feel that bit more meaningful.
As always, we recommend joining our community on Discord to organise match-ups!
In relevant multiplayer modes, the break is now decided by the Lag, bringing Pure Pool Pro closer to real-world play.

If you’re unfamiliar with the term, in pro pool, the lag is used to decide who breaks. Both players hit a cue ball from behind the headstring up-table, aiming to get as close as possible to the top rail and back without touching a pocket. The player whose ball finishes closest to the rail wins the lag - and with it, the right to choose who breaks.
Both players take their lag attempts
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/55ba186e152a1814761e7b561d116983c7b8f8bc.gif"]
You’ll then be shown your attempt side-by-side with your opponent’s (in ghost ball form if playing online).
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/6523ec9db5a6bf93113f5920509c0cc30e4cf071.gif"]
The closest ball to the head rail wins, and that player can decide to take the break themselves or pass it to their opponent.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/c1d108b9c28cc72c84f2a3ae84d330e2780e1855.gif"]
Should both players foul (or, in the unlikely event of lagging in the exact spot), a re-lag will take place.
This should make the opening of each match feel fairer, add a more skill-based/tactical element, and make things more authentic to how things work on real tables.

notes.title: Ball Shadow Pop Fix & Restored Gloss

items.text: Since launch, we’ve been working to the ball “shadow pop” - distracting little jumps in lighting and shadow as balls came to rest. Pure Pool Pro uses a much more advanced and demanding reflections system compared to its predecessor, and this visual issue has been a tough nut for us to crack!
With Patch 3, we’ve made notable improvements.
Shadow “pop” and reflection instability on balls have been dramatically reduced
We’ve also reintroduced the glossy and vivid look of the balls, which was unintentionally dialled back/desaturated during earlier attempts to fix the issue
The result should be cleaner, more stable reflections with that satisfying, polished finish many of you loved - without the distracting artefacts.
PRE-PATCH 3 VISUALS
Community noted that previous shadow pop fix attempts had reduced the glossiness for a ‘matte’ look.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/c3c40f22dd4895c511758b19c882ca39332d3c97.jpg"]
PATCH 3 VISUALS - ARRIVING 21st MAY
Enhanced reflections and richer, warmer colour restoring that ‘glossy’ look - with more stable performance.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/eef887e9058e73d5154ba5d77c995b3dabd4d155.jpg"]
We’ll continue to monitor feedback here, but we feel this represents a major step toward the visual standard we’ve been chasing.
Alongside the ball shadow and gloss improvements, Patch 3 will deliver smoother overall frame pacing and increased frame rate stability across both console and PC.
While the core goal of these changes was visual fidelity, the underlying optimisations have:
Reduced minor hitches and stutters related to ball reflections and lighting, most notably at the break
Improved consistency of performance during busy table states

The result should be a more fluid, reliable experience that better matches the precision and responsiveness Pure Pool Pro is built around - whether you’re playing on a high-end PC or from the comfort of your home console.

notes.title: 9-Ball Push Outs - A New Tactical Layer

items.text: In 9-Ball, we’ve implemented proper Push Out functionality.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/9fd45a890d9239eff2c44ea811e229fc36681380.gif"]

After a legal break in 9-Ball, the incoming player can now choose to play a push out - making contact with the cue ball without the usual requirement to hit the lowest-numbered ball first or to drive a ball to a cushion.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/6fc533d306e64a42c55a41227e58701d40c1b251.gif"]
Push Outs are only available immediately after a legal break
After a push out, your opponent can choose to take on the shot from the new position or pass the shot back to you
This adds a deeper tactical layer to 9-Ball, especially in high-pressure frames where controlling the table and leaving awkward layouts can be just as important as potting!
“Freeplay” will now remember your difficulty preference upon launching the game
“Clarence Clearance” has been fixed for those who were struggling to pop the crest
“Accumulator” rule tweak - this mode will now permit sequential potting
Steam Controller API now ensures correct icons are used for your chosen controller
Steam Controller API now permits re-mapping of gamepad controls via the Steam overlay
We’ve tweaked the “Match Preferences” flow to make “Preferences” clearer

notes.title: Thank You For Your Continued Support!

items.text: Patch 3 arrives next week as a result of your continued detailed feedback - on ranked systems, rulesets, QoL, and visuals. Every detailed review, Reddit post, and Discord message genuinely helps us decide what to prioritise next.
We’re thrilled to get these changes into your hands and to keep pushing Pure Pool Pro forward.
If you enjoy next week’s patch and want to help us continue to support the game and keep building the community, please consider leaving/or updating a Steam review.
We’ll see you at the table.
The Pure Pool Pro Team 🎱

items.text: Hello again, Pool Fans,
Our Month 1 Patch is now live on both PC and Console.
For the best possible experience, be sure to update your game before you next play.
Here’s what’s included in this patch;
Competitive Stats - Statistics are now shown on Player Cards at the beginning of online matches: Games Won, Games Lost, Win Ratio %, and Win Streak. Additional stats available in the “Socials” Menu.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/aefb3ad512c08059cd26ccbde51bc1080049a41e.png"]

Star Unlock Criteria Adjustments - Certain challenges throughout the career have been rebalanced and made more forgiving to better reflect their intended difficulty. Notably, challenges involving specific potting distances and multiple pots will now reward you if you exceed the challenge, too.
Rule Adjustment: Potting the 8-Ball from the Break in US 8-Ball was considered a Foul - Now, if the player pots the 8-Ball on the break, the player re-racks and takes the break again.
Checkpoint Timing Adjustments - We’ve made some minor tweaks to the timing behaviour to allow for final buzzer-beating shots.
Power Feather Added to FTUX - We’d noticed a lot of players were unaware of this function, so explanation text for the ‘Power Feather’ mechanic has now been added to the tutorial.
AI Opponent Profiles - Short bios have been added to the “Profiles” of each AI opponent in the Versus menu, with details on their playing styles as well as their signature cue and how to unlock it.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45586874/4d3ccdebf1f7dd70a9af3fc2a39e2bc57a34d0d9.png"]
AI Behaviour Tweaks - We’re continuing to adjust our AI opponent behaviours following Hotfix 1. Further reduced instances of AI players accidentally potting ‘flukey’ shots.
Career Completion Tweak - Added congratulatory messaging for completing each career path. An additional credit roll sequence will trigger upon completing the ‘Pro’ career path.
Sub Menu Navigation Functionality - Improved navigation when browsing the Equipment, Crest, and Player Card menus.

Stand-Up Interaction Fix - Fixed a bug where players could not stand up or adjust spin while a music track notification was visible. The user can now observe the table or reset the spin whilst the notification is present.
Baize Decal Sub Menu Added - Added dedicated sub menus for baize decals, which are now sorted by category.
Aim Guide Clipping Fix - Addressed some edge case visual clipping issues with the aim guide on both ‘Amateur’ and ‘Focused’ settings.
‘Money Shot’ Visual Improvements - Adjusted the visual presentation and timing of the Money Shot moments.

(Ongoing) Reflection Stability Optimisation - Made optimisations to reduce the “shadow pop” issue on balls. These 'pops' are now less frequent in most scenarios further up the table - but still apparent when balls come to rest at the near end of the table. Work is ongoing.
Cue and Table Audio Enhancements
Improved break and ball impact sounds
Refined pocket and table mechanism sounds
Added reactive audience sounds in the Tetradome arena
Smoother soundtrack transitions between menus and gameplay
Headphone Audio Fix - Reduced ‘crackle’/’interference’ reported on some headphones.

Steam Deck and Handheld PC Optimisations – Pure Pool Pro now detects popular handheld PCs such as Steam Deck, ASUS ROG Ally and Lenovo Legion Go, and runs with new device-specific profiles on each. These profiles apply adjusted anti-aliasing, optimal resolution settings, bespoke reflections, and GPU tweaks to deliver better performance and a smoother experience on handhelds that meet the system requirements.
PC Framerate Optimisations - General framerate improvements on PC.
PS5 Framerate Optimisations - General performance improvements on PlayStation 5 and PS5 Pro.

20+ New National Flags for your Player Card - We’ve added an assortment of new national flags for player cards, based on the countries in which Pure Pool Pro is most popular. Want your country’s flag in-game? Be sure to let us know!
DLC Store Added - A new in-game DLC store has been introduced, accessible via the main menu.
DLC Free Item Pack - Our complimentary “Free Item Pack” is now available to all players. Including a new ball set, 4x Player Cards, 5x Baize Designs, and a Premium Animated Crest.

Hello again, Pool Fans,
We’ve been closely monitoring feedback around AI opponents - particularly concerns about unrealistic multi-rail pots, fluke misses dropping in, and shots that simply didn’t feel believable.
While broader AI tuning remains part of our Month 1 Patch in March, we’ve moved quickly to deploy a targeted hotfix addressing the most egregious behaviours.
This update is live now on Steam and PlayStation.
We’ve implemented two significant changes to shot logic and outcome validation:
The Issue

When the AI missed a shot, there was no secondary validation to prevent the miss from unintentionally potting another ball. This led to a frustratingly high frequency of “I missed… but it went in anyway” moments.
What We’ve Changed
AI misses are now checked to ensure they have a far lower probability of accidentally potting another ball.
This should significantly reduce unrealistic fluke outcomes.
The Issue
AI shot selection works via weighted categories (e.g. all our players have different probabilities of straight pots, banks, kicks, plants, and “crazy” shots).
Previously, bank and kick shots were categorised as such regardless of how many rails were involved.

This meant extreme multi-rail attempts could be selected far more often than we intended - resulting in a lot of outrageous, highlight-reel style pots (that a lot of you will have seen in vids posted on Reddit and YouTube!).
What We’ve Changed
Any shot involving more than one rail is now classified as a “Crazy” shot; a value used for our AI's attempting a shot that would be considered out-of-the-ordinary.
Most AI opponents now have only a 0–8% chance of ever attempting a Crazy shot.
This change has dramatically reduced unrealistic multi-rail conversions and improbable snooker escapes.
AI Player Ermina Merdanović remains the exception, with her Crazy shot percentage notably higher than that of other players. This is an intentional choice to reflect her distinct playing style.

notes.title: In summary, these changes should result in

items.text: Far fewer “impossible” feeling pots
Reduced fluke behaviour
More believable shot selection
More realistic AI escapes from snookers
This, however, is not the final word on AI - and we want to be clear about that.

AI tuning is something we will continue refining over time based on feedback and data. The Month 1 Patch will include more difficulty curve and behaviour adjustments, but this hotfix directly targets the issues causing the most frustration right now.
If this update improves your experience, please consider updating your review so it reflects the current state of the game. It genuinely helps us reach more players and continue long-term support.
We understand how strongly people feel about competitive fairness in offline play. Thank you to everyone who raised concerns constructively - and please keep the feedback coming.
See you at the table

Based on your feedback since launch, we've tried to target the most reported issues as fast as we could.
Here’s what’s changing in this patch
CAMERA FIX – Too Close to Cue Ball & Off-Centre Aiming
The Issue

Many players - especially on Pro difficulty without aim lines - reported difficulty lining up shots. This was worsened when forced cue elevation caused the camera to shift (most noticeable near rails).
We pushed for realism here. In practice, the camera shifting off-centre made shot judgment far harder than intended.
What We’ve Done
• The camera is now permanently centred in all scenarios - even when the cue is elevated
• The camera has been moved much further back from the cue ball to improve overall table readability in all scenarios

This should dramatically improve shot alignment and Pro-level playability, particularly near cushions. If you've gotten used to the current camera, please do give yourself a little time to readjust - we think it's worthwhile.

Please note: We are continuing to review expanded camera options based on your feedback and hope to provide more options and customisability, but this will require comprehensive testing and additional work. More on that soon.
CONTROL FIX – Mouse Sensitivity Overhaul
The Issue
Players experienced overly high or “twitchy” mouse sensitivity at certain DPI ranges, making feathered or gentle shots unreliable. Our mouse sensitivity scaling was out of whack!
What We’ve Done
• Reworked mouse sensitivity scaling
• Improved power consistency
• Enhanced fine shot control
Lining up shots and gauging stroke strength should now more intuitive for mouse users.
VISUAL FIX – Ball Reflection “Pop” / “Flicker”
The Issue
Our most reported visual issue since launch.
Reflections on balls were refreshing at slightly different rates, causing a noticeable “pop” or flicker - particularly in Rackhaus and on certain baize designs.
What We’ve Done
Implemented several lighting and reflection adjustments
Reduced the shadow/reflection popping effect
Improvements apply across platforms
UI FIX – Aim Guide Clipping (Royal Rumble)
The Issue
In Royal Rumble, the floating object ball could block the aim guide, making lines unreadable.
What We’ve Done
• Aim guides now pass cleanly through the floating ball
ADDITIONAL FIXES - Achievements
Players reported issues with the following achievements, which we have now fixed.
Fixed “Crest Conqueror” achievement
